theme: 3 terms on a view's geometry: its place in the parent, its own space, and the effect that changes how it is drawn

terms.definition: The position and size of a view, measured in its parent's coordinates.
terms.example: Print the Frame to see where the view really is.

terms.definition: A view's own position and size, measured in its own coordinates, so the origin is usually zero.
terms.example: Use the Bounds to draw inside the view, not the parent's space.

terms.definition: A value that rotates, scales or moves a view without changing its layout.
terms.example: Rotate the arrow with a Transform, the layout stays the same.

video.title: Frame, Bounds & Transform | Day 100
video.description:
Learn to explain why a view reports different sizes: Frame, Bounds & Transform, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Frame - The position and size of a view, measured in its parent's coordinates.
Bounds - A view's own position and size, measured in its own coordinates, so the origin is usually zero.
Transform - A value that rotates, scales or moves a view without changing its layout.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Frame or Bounds? Can you explain the difference in English?

dialogue.title: Two different widths

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I scaled the card, but its width changed in one place and not in another.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Frame got twice as wide. The Bounds stayed the same.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's expected. A Transform changes how the view is drawn, so the Frame follows it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. The Bounds describe the view's own space, before the Transform.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the Frame is the position in the parent view.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Use the Frame to place the view, and the Bounds to draw inside it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if the view is rotated?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the Frame is the box around the rotated shape. Don't set it directly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. I'll use constraints instead.

dialogue.code:
print(card.frame.width)
card.transform = CGAffineTransform(
    scaleX: 2, y: 2)
print(card.frame.width)
print(card.bounds.width)
